title: SDK developer ergonomics: progressive call adapters for streamed tool schemas (ts/py/go)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver language idiomatic SDK adapters that make progressive (streaming) tool/function invocations ergonomically consistent across TypeScript, Python, and Go while preserving typed structured output and backwards compatibility with existing sync/invocation patterns.

Problem statement: Teams building on Redwood API are implementing ad-hoc streaming handlers for tool/function calls and structured outputs. This leads to duplication, fragile backpressure handling, and divergent developer ergonomics between TS/Py/Go. We need a small, well-specified set of adapter interfaces and example patterns to: unify behavior, guide customers on migration, and reduce runtime integration bugs.

Scope:
- Public SDK surface: adapters for progressive tool invocation and typed streaming outputs in TS/py/go.
- Examples and recipes for common patterns (tool multiplexing, backpressure, schema validation, partial-result aggregation).
- Migration guide for legacy sync-style invocations and existing streaming hooks.
- Tests: unit tests for adapters + end-to-end sample app per language.

Out of scope: changes to runtime protocol beyond current streaming/event envelope, deep performance rework of batching kernels (tracked in infra roadmap).
acceptance_criteria: Language-specific adapter modules (ts/py/go) that expose consistent developer APIs for consuming streamed tool events and structured outputs
Integration examples (one small demo app per language) that show tool-calling, function return schemas, and progressive partial results aggregation
Backwards-compatible defaults so existing sync invocations continue to work without code changes
Automated tests that validate schema typing and backpressure behavior in CI
Docs and migration guide published in SDK docs site and linked from Console docs
design_decisions: Expose a small core runtime-agnostic adapter interface (OnEvent, OnSchemaError, OnComplete, Cancel) and provide language idiomatic wrappers (async iterators for TS/Py, channel-based consumer for Go)
Preserve the current streaming event envelope shape; adapters should map events to typed emits rather than changing wire protocol
Schema validation is opt-in by default to avoid runtime overhead for high-throughput paths; enable with boolean flag or helper that returns a validated stream
Default buffering window is minimal (1 event) and adapters provide explicit buffering helpers for aggregation use-cases
Provide a compatibility shim layer that translates legacy sync callbacks into the progressive adapter surface for existing customers
implementation_notes: TS: provide AsyncGenerator<TypedToolEvent> wrapper and convenience helpers to convert to Rx/observable patterns used by some consumers
Python: support async generator and sync iterator wrappers; include an iterator that yields validated pydantic models for structured outputs
Go: design a channel-based consumer with cancellable context and a small helper that materializes final typed result structs
All three languages should ship a small example: 'invoice-extractor' that calls a tool which emits partial JSON schema fragments and a final merged typed object
Performance: adapters must avoid unnecessary copies; tests should assert <5% overhead on synthetic streaming microbenchmarks compared to bare event loop
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter behavior (event ordering, cancel path, schema error handling)
Integration E2E tests using the hosted API test harness to assert progressive delivery and final typed output
Fuzz tests for malformed streaming envelopes to ensure adapters surface schema errors without crashing the host process
CI gates: add runtime smoke to SDK CI matrix for each language (linux, mac)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): ship TS adapters and examples to npm @redwood/sdk-canary, docs behind feature flag; gather feedback from 3 internal teams
Phase 2: ship Python adapters to PyPI and Go module; update Console docs and example templates
Phase 3: GA release, migration guide, deprecation notes for legacy helpers
Monitor: track number of customers who adopt progressive adapters and errors surfaced by schema-validator; roll back flag if urgent regressions found
